ambiguities.text: The EIP does not specify when exactly the size check should occur in the block validation pipeline
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume size check occurs early in validation, before expensive operations like signature verification, to prevent DoS. This is the security-optimal interpretation.

ambiguities.text: The relationship between MAX_BLOCK_SIZE (10 MiB) and MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE (8 MiB) and how the 2 MiB safety margin accommodates beacon layer constraints is not precisely defined
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the 2 MiB margin accounts for beacon block wrapper overhead and potential variations in encoding. Exact CL constraint should be verified against consensus specs.

implicit_assumptions.description: The consensus layer has a block size limit of approximately 10 MiB that would reject blocks exceeding this limit regardless of EL validation
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If CL limit is different, the safety margin may be insufficient or overly conservative, potentially causing valid blocks to be rejected or oversized blocks to reach CL

implicit_assumptions.description: All client implementations will implement this check consistently at the same point in their validation pipeline
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Inconsistent implementation timing could lead to some clients being vulnerable to resource exhaustion attacks while others are protected

implicit_assumptions.description: Validators have incentive to construct blocks within the size limit due to rejection risk
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Validators who ignore the limit will have their blocks rejected network-wide, wasting their block production opportunity
